title: Optimize / Evals 1:1 prep - quality regressions & A/B results
content:
Purpose:
- Prep notes for weekly 1:1 with Jamie (optimize/evals). Focus: recent quality regressions surfaced by monitors, A/B results from last rollout, and prompt-set health.

TL;DR:
- Two small regressions detected on v3.2.1 (chat-completion) in the "summarize-legal" and "qa-short" prompt sets. Impact: ~0.8% drop in accept rate for summarize-legal, ~1.4% for qa-short on production traffic.
- A/B: canary (v3.2.1 + quant profile B) shows ~0.3% latency gain but mixed quality for edge cases.
- Hypothesis: quant profile B + new tokenizer changes interacting with prompt prefixes for long inputs -> subtle context truncation/formatting differences.

Quick metrics snapshot (last 7d):
- summarize-legal: baseline accept 92.4% -> current 91.6% (n=23k)
- qa-short: baseline 95.7% -> current 94.3% (n=18k)
- average p95 latency: baseline 420ms -> current 405ms (canary gain ~3.6%)
- cost per token (est): down ~4% on canary

Agenda (items I want to cover):
1) Walk through regressions (summarize-legal, qa-short) — show a couple of failing examples (I'll bring 3 each).
2) A/B summary & what to keep/drop from quant profile B.
3) Prompt set hygiene: recent edits, agent injection risk, tokenization edge cases.
4) Action items: triage plan, short-term mitigations, rollout gating criteria.
5) Quick sync on evaluation harness (test coverage gaps + missing synthetic cases).

Notes / talking points:
- Regressions are small but persistent across time windows; not a single noise spike. Worth triage because legal summarization has higher business risk.
- Examples: summarize-legal failures are mostly formatting/omission (missing clause paraphrase). qa-short failures are hallucinations on numeric facts in short Q/A.
- Correlation with release timeline: regression coincides with tokenizer patch (PR #445) + quant profile B rollout on dedicated. Both landed same week.
- Canary vs prod split: canary traffic skewed towards US-EN, might mask region-specific tokens (e.g., special unicode in EU contracts).

Hypotheses to test (quick):
- Tokenizer change altered byte-to-token mapping for certain punctuation sequences -> prompt prefix + system messages get shifted; prompts exceed effective context -> model drops end of input.
- Quant profile B increases rounding noise in logits for low-prob tokens -> more likely to drop rare entity tokens -> hallucinations in qa-short.
- Serving runtime batching changed around same time (auto-batching tweak) -> KV cache reuse boundary bug.

What I will bring to meeting (attachments / artifacts):
- 6 failing examples (3 per prompt set) with diff between baseline and current outputs.
- A/B metrics dashboard snapshot (7d + 24h) + per-region breakdown.
- Tokenization diffs for failing examples (baseline vs new tokenizer).

Immediate triage plan (proposal):
- Roll back quant profile B for affected model family on production (if we see continued regression) but keep canary for internal perf testing. Owner: Aisha. Target: 2026-03-06 if we confirm.
- Add synthetic unit tests for summarize-legal: include long-contract samples with edge punctuation. Owner: me (Samir) + Jamie. Due: 2026-03-10.
- Add tokenization check to preflight for any tokenizer change: sample tokenization parity on canonical prompt sets. Owner: infra-team (PR request). Due: 2026-03-12.
- Short-term mitigation: increase prefix safety margin for summarize-legal (truncate earlier) to avoid clipping. Owner: Product / Prompt owners. Due: 2026-03-05.

Action items to confirm in 1:1 (assignments to sync):
- Jamie: confirm whether any other model families reported similar small drops (esp. dedicated customers).
- Aisha: run ablation of quant profile B by toggling only quant (keep tokenizer constant) and share outputs for the failing examples. Due: 2026-03-06.
- Samir (me): add failing examples to the eval harness + write quick synthetic cases. Due: 2026-03-10.
- Infra (ask via ticket): add tokenization parity check to CI for tokenizer PRs. Reference: CONFLUENCE-OPTIMIZE-245.

Open questions / unresolved: 
- Is this regression customer-visible beyond our accept-rate metric? (I need Jamie to forward any CS/AE tickets).
- Could locale-specific unicode behavior explain EU contract failures? Need per-region tokenization audit.
- Is KV cache boundary plausible? Where are batching logs (SRE pointer)?

Back-of-envelope risk matrix:
- High risk: summarize-legal regressions (legal correctness/omission) -> escalate to product if trend continues.
- Medium risk: qa-short hallucinations (user annoyance + small coverage).
- Low risk: slight latency improvement (nice to have).

Prep checklist (what I will do before meeting):
- [x] Pull 3 failing examples per prompt set
- [x] Export A/B dashboard (7d + 24h)
- [ ] Run tokenization diffs and attach outputs
- [ ] Draft rollback playbook in case regressions widen

Meeting goals:
- Come out with 3 clear next steps and owners + dates.
- Decide whether to hold canary or roll back quant profile B for prod.
- Agree on additional synthetic tests to prevent recurrence.

Misc notes / quick links:
- Related PRs: tokenizer PR #445, quant profile B PR #460, batch tweak PR #452
- Jira: JIRA-ML-1023 (regression triage), JIRA-OPS-778 (batch logs)
